What degraded

  • Shipped at the round cap at 7.45, 0.25 under the 7.7 rung and 0.55 under the 8.0 top rung.
  • Round 5's hard fail (an unscoped universal about which answers the engine reads first) was repaired after the cards and verified by four integrity-only passes, not by a sixth scoring round.
  • No rescore dates or fee amount. The agency's scoring document names a window and points to its Calendar of Events, and the run did not fetch that calendar.
  • Eight record items stay unconfirmed behind hosts that refuse the project or every client. reverify.py fetched two refused hosts again and its stamps were withdrawn.
  • The scanner ceiling was not checked. This run has no D1 or Worker settings access.
  • The September 27th article prints a doubled percent sign. That is shipped history, left for a maintainer.

Named here rather than left out. A run that quietly ships less than it planned teaches nobody anything.

Post this

Upload the PDF to LinkedIn as a document, title it A machine reads it first. How Texas scores written STAAR, paste the post copy under it, then paste the first comment within a minute of posting.

carousel.pdf   contact sheet   the site

1. The post copy

Who reads a long written STAAR answer first?

Unless the test is in Spanish, a machine does. The Texas Education Agency has done it that way since December 2023. In the agency's chart the machine's score stands on about 75% of them. The agency said scoring them all by hand would have cost $15 million to $20 million more a year.

The machine learned from about 3,000 human scored answers per question. Low confidence scores, blank answers and a random sample go to people, and the person's score counts.

The agency said about 27,200 students got more credit on the reading test after content experts reread short typed answers. It said the engine scored none of them.

A parent can take a concern to the district. Its testing staff can request a human rescore for a fee. If the score changes, the fee is waived.

Should a family have to ask for a person?

#STAAR #TexasEducationAgency #TexasSchools

The machine changed itself

  • Kit person poses read and sit_read, and no skin through a short sleeve
    All three round 1 judges named that no reader was reading. Every later card read them as reading.
  • student_desk and student_desk_rows in the kit, one bent tube per side frame
    Round 1's craft card named the hero as a separate desk and chair with stub posts.
  • The kit school shades its own covered walk
    Three judges read the facade as a flat card. The chassis's shade had landed 6.53 m off the wall.
  • classroom_window in the kit
    Frame 5's blown white pane was round 5's top artwork defect.
  • Backlog, top item: window openings in TXT.interior (engine, human lane)
    Frame 5's room can't get a real window with light through it without an engine change.

Every change is logged in ledger/carousel/upgrades.json.

Notes

THE ENGINE FIX FIRST, a backlog proposal for a maintainer. Frame 5's classroom was round 5's top artwork defect. A real window opening with light through it needs an openings option on TXT.interior in assets/js/txthree.js, which is human lane. It is item 0 in knowledge/carousel/UPGRADE_BACKLOG.md. The record: 45 items re-verified and stamped. 8 are left unconfirmed with dated notes, behind hosts that refuse the project's agent or every client. reverify.py fetched tacc.utexas.edu and public.destinyhosted.com again, so its stamps on tx-2026-0125 and tx-2026-0168 to 0170 were withdrawn, for the third run running. Admitted tx-2026-0194, the Texas Education Agency's hybrid scoring of STAAR constructed responses, from the agency's own scoring process and key questions documents and the Tribune's September 4th account. The deck ships at the round cap at 7.45. Rounds were 6.924, 7.18, 7.19, 7.40 and 7.45. Round 5's integrity judge failed the web edition for saying the engine is the first reader of every written answer, which the run's own claims refute. It was repaired on the web edition, the record item, the cover dek and the caption, and verified by four integrity-only passes. Each of the first three found a surface the last repair had missed. Permission prompts: prompt_audit exits 1 and counts 503 of 1,744 calls over one second. 1,214 took under 100 ms, 456 took 1 to 2 s, 46 took 2 to 5 s, and one Bash call took 10.5 s at 09:36 UTC. The no-stall hook was armed, judged the session unattended with the host's own CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ATTENDED=0, refused nothing and logged no dialog. Hundreds of one to three second waits in an unattended session look like the host's decision latency, not a person. The upgrade phase proposed counting a wait as human only when the hook logged a dialog for it. Post it knowing that slide 9 names the rescore window's source but not its dates, because the run did not fetch the agency's Calendar of Events.

This is a draft. Nothing was sent. The deck is already merged to main, so these links are live. Posting is the only step left, and it is yours.
